title.en: From a slow girl to a strong woman

text.en: A little girl is called Bholi, a simpleton. A teacher changes her life.

The story is by K. A. Abbas. Bholi's real name is Sulekha, the youngest of Ramlal's children, and she is slow and has a stammer after an illness.
At home she is ignored and treated as a burden, wearing her sisters' old clothes.
When the school opens, Ramlal takes her there to be admitted, since no one wants to marry such a girl.
Her kind teacher encourages her and treats her with love. Bholi slowly gains confidence and learns to speak.
Years later a well-to-do grocer, Bishamber Nath, who is older and limps, offers to marry her without asking for dowry, and her parents agree.
At the wedding Bholi, who had been willing for the sake of her family's honour, refuses to marry a man she calls mean, greedy and a coward.
She says she will teach in the school where she learnt so much and serve her parents.
The story shows the power of education to give confidence and courage, especially to girls.

problem.en: Bholi is the youngest of 4 sisters. If she is 10 and each sister is 2 years older than the next, how old is the eldest?

text.en: Add 2 years for each of the three older sisters.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking Bholi was slow by nature
